items.title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None

items.title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL issues up to ~112k KV descriptors per rank-transfer, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**.

The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's.

Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below.

### Measurements

GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion.

| Transport | Descriptors / transfer | Post mean | Total mean | Movement remainder | Payload / remainder | Post share |

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scales
items.bodyExcerpt:
# Fix the SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scale mismatch

## Summary

This change rounds each `fp8_ds_mla` tile scale up to an E8M0-compatible
power of two on SM100 and later GPUs.

The change applies to both cache writers:

- the native CUDA writer;
- the fused DeepSeek-V3.2 Triton writer.

## Problem

Each writer used an arbitrary 32-bit floating-point (FP32) scale to quantize
an E4M3 tile. The writer then stored this FP32 scale in the cache.

On SM100, FlashMLA converts the stored scale to E8M0 before dequantization.
Thus, FlashMLA used a different scale from the writer. This mismatch increased
the dequantization error.

The change rounds the scale up before quantization. The writer and FlashMLA
now use the same scale. Rounding down could make the largest tile value
overflow E4M3.

GPUs before SM100 keep the existing behavior.

items.title: [rocm] perf: drop redundant -inf prefill of decode paged MQA-logits buffer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Removes the full-width `out_logits.fill_(float("-inf"))` before the decode paged MQA-logits kernel in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`).

The decode consumer, `top_k_per_row_decode`, bounds its per-row scan by `seq_lens` (it reads only `[0, rowEnd)` where `rowEnd = seq_len - next_n + next_n_idx + 1`) and pads short rows (`rowLen <= topK`) with `-1` internally. The paged MQA-logits kernels write every in-causal column that top-k reads:
- Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes `-inf` into masked in-tile positions itself.
- FlyDSL `flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes exactly `col <= q_limit` (== the columns top-k reads).

So the out-of-window `[rowEnd, max_model_len)` region initialized by this `fill_` is never consumed on the decode path, making the prefill redundant. Dropping it saves a `rows x max_model_len` fp32 HBM write every decode step.

## Why it's safe (decode path)

`q_limit` (kernel write extent) and `rowEnd` (top-k read extent) are both derived from the same context length and `next_n`, so every column top-k reads is freshly written; nothing reads the untouched tail.

## Scope / caveats

- Only affects the **decode** paged path (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`).
- The prefill top-k path and the `topk_indices_buffer[...] = -1` init are untouched.
- The FlyDSL kernel documents a `-inf`-prefill contract; this change relies on the consumer's `seq_lens` bounding rather than the kernel self-initializing, so it should be validated numerically.

## Test plan

- [ ] Compare decode top-k indices with/without the fill across short / long / padded batches (Gluon and FlyDSL paths) on gfx942/gfx950.
- [ ] Run existing `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` and sparse-indexer tests.
- [ ] Sanity-check end-to-end GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA decode output.

## Purpose

Fixes #51080.

`pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call. A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` no matter how much host memory is free, so `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 is never pinned. Measured on 4×H200 NVL with 1.3 TB free, one process, no model loaded:

| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |

## Summary

After [vllm#49714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49714), every decode step runs `nan_to_num_(-inf)` over the full

## Purpose

Fuse the clamped MoE activation path into FP8 block-128 activation quantization:

1. finite SwiGLU clamping;
2. BF16 SiLU and gated multiplication;
3. dynamic E4M3 block quantization, including Hopper DeepGEMM UE8M0 scales; and
4. optional filtering of invalid or non-local expert rows.

- a lightweight one-block-per-quant-group kernel for launch-bound TP decode shapes without an `expert_map`;

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] GLM-4.7: stray arg tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
`compute_block_transfer_offsets` in the MoRI-IO KV connector raised `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` whenever the producer's local block count exceeded the consumer's. Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** with `block_size=1`, the prefill (producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead slots that the decode (consumer) side does not allocate, so `local` exceeds `remote` by exactly the spec-token count (e.g. **8003 vs 8000** at n=3). This crashed the first prefill→decode KV write and made MTP unusable over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation.

## Fix
Block order is positional (`block_size=1`), so the prompt KV is the prefix and the extra local blocks are empty lookahead scratch. Clamp `local_block_ids` to `local[:len(remote)]` and transfer only the prompt prefix — symmetric with the existing shorter-local handling already documented in the same function.

- Replaces the now-obsolete longer-local *raise* test with **clamp-to-prompt-prefix** tests for both the interleaved (`transfers_per_block=1`) and separated split-KV (`transfers_per_block=2`) layouts, asserting the result is identical to transferring `local[:len(remote)]`.

items.title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Use FlashKDA for KDA chunked prefill (1.7-3.8x faster than the Triton chunk path)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Use **FlashKDA** (`vllm._flashkda_C`, already built and used by Kimi-K3) for GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA chunked prefill instead of the ~15-kernel Triton `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` path.

FlashKDA implements the same bounded-gate KDA recurrence GLM-5.3-Flash uses (`lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (g + dt_bias))`, in-kernel q/k l2norm, raw beta logits), so it is a drop-in. On GB300 per KDA layer (H=16/rank, D=128, `bench/flashkda_vs_chunk.py`):

| shape | Triton chunk path | FlashKDA |
|---|---|---|
| 8 x 2048 tokens | 183 us | 49 us |
| 4 x 8192 | 555 us | 146 us |
| 1 x 16384 | 1371 us | 787 us |

Selection: automatic when supported (SM90/SM10x/SM12x, bf16, head_dim 128, bounded gate); `additional_config.kda_prefill_backend = triton` keeps the old path (`flashkda` forces it). The output is written straight into the layer buffer (no merge copy) and the pre-sigmoid beta cast is not needed on this path. Spec-decode tokens themselves keep the Triton recurrent kernel (`num_accepted_tokens` rollback); in a step that carries both, FlashKDA runs the prefill segment into a workspace buffer and the outputs are scattered back by `non_spec_token_indx` / `spec_token_indx` (same scheme as the Kimi-K3 KDA layer; the merge writes straight into `core_attn_out`).

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Poolside: stray arg_key tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`PoolsideV1ToolParser.func_arg_regex` captures the argument key with a plain
`.*?`:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>", re.DOTALL
)
```

A non-greedy `.*?` guarantees only the *shortest match consistent with the
rest of the pattern*, not that it stops at the first literal `</arg_key>`.
If `\s*<arg_value>` fails to match right after that first occurrence, the
engine backtracks and lets `.*?` cross the boundary to reach a *later*
`</arg_key>`, silently absorbing a stray `<arg_key>`/`</arg_key>` tag into
the parsed key.

This is the identical defect class and identical fix shape as the GLM-4.7
leak fixed in #54971 (reviewer Manny7717 flagged this exact call site in
that PR's review, at `vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py:82`).
The fix bounds the key to runs of non-`<` text, so the capture group can
never cross its own delimiter:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>([^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
    r"<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

This file uses the third-party `regex` module (`import regex as re`), not
stdlib `re` — `regex` has always supported possessive quantifiers (`*+`)
regardless of interpreter version, so (unlike a stdlib-`re` site) no
non-possessive fallback is needed here. The repo's `requires-python` floor
is `>=3.10,<3.15`; the dev venv used for testing runs 3.13.15, and a
20,000-case randomized differential check (see Test Result) against the
old pattern found no divergence on well-formed input and no leaked `<` in
malformed input.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs against `poolside`/`arg_key`/`tool_parsers` before
starting. The only overlapping PR is #54678
("[Bugfix][Security] Fix catastrophic backtracking in the poolside_v1 and
dots tool-call regexes"), which is **not** a duplicate of this fix: it
targets a different defect class (ReDoS/timing) in the *same file*'s

items.title: [ROCm] [Bugfix] Enable Load and Inference of GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 Checkpoint
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The Quark checkpoint `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, global MXFP4 quant with attention projections kept as source block-FP8/BF16). Two independent bugs break weight load. This PR fixes both and the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint now loads and serves with accuracy on par with the source checkpoint (`zai/GLM-5.3-Flash`).

## Bugs

1. Dense-MLP `gate_up_proj` resolves to the wrong quant scheme:
The class inherits `packed_modules_mapping = {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]}` from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration`. This identity mapping is correct for GLM-4.1V (whose checkpoint stores a pre-fused `gate_up_proj` tensor), but GLM-5.3-Flash stores gate/up as **separate** tensors (both the [Quark ](https://huggingface.co/amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4)and the [base](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) checkpoints). With the identity entry, `QuarkConfig` falls back to `global_quant_config` (MXFP4) instead of the per-layer block-FP8 in `layer_quant_config` and builds the layer as MXFP4 and mismatches the FP8 checkpoint tensor at load.


2. MLA projection scale name mismatch:
The MLA `q_a` / `kv_a` / `q_b` / `o` projections are dequantized on load by `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, which only recognized scales named `weight_scale_inv`. Quark checkpoints export `weight_scale`, so the scale fell through and the fused-qkv-a stacked mapping could not find its target.

## Changes (`vllm/model_executor/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`)

1. Override `packed_modules_mapping` on `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` so the  fused `gate_up_proj` expands to its real shard names `["gate_proj", "up_proj"]` (matching the `Glm4vMoeForConditionalGeneration` sibling / `glm4_moe` / `deepseek_v2`).
2. In `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, accept the Quark scale name:
   `is_scale = "weight_scale_inv" in name or name.endswith(".weight_scale")`.

## Related PRs and Issues:

Bug 1 was initially reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add a version-aware merged-weight cache key in the KDA layer
- rebuild the merged tensor when any source conv weight changes
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache
- invoke cache invalidation before GLM-5.3 weight loading so the next access rebuilds from fresh weights

Make MTP reachable for PCP+DCP sparse-MLA prefillers behind NIXL P/D.

items.title: [Security] Cap Qwen-VL video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL video samplers ignore `num_frames` and bound sampling on request-controlled `max_frames` and `fps`. A client can raise those knobs through `media_io_kwargs` and force the frontend to decode every source frame. This applies the same class-level ceilings already used by the GLMGA sampler (`_MAX_FRAMES`, `_MAX_FPS`), so a request may lower the sample count but cannot raise it past 768 frames or 30 fps.

## Changes
- `vllm/multimodal/video.py`: clamp `max_frames` and `fps` in `Qwen2VLVideoBackend` and `Qwen3VLVideoBackend`.

## Codepath coverage
- Sink is `compute_frames_index_to_sample` on both Qwen backends. OpenCV, TorchCodec, PyNvVideoCodec, and DeepStream all call that method, so every codec is covered.
- Chat completions, embeddings, responses, tokenize, invocations, batch, and offline `LLM` all reach the same `MediaConnector` → `VideoMediaIO` → registered sampler chain.
- `video/jpeg` `load_base64` does not use these samplers (it keys off `num_frames`). The Rust frontend rejects `media_io_kwargs` and is unaffected.
- Sibling loaders (Molmo2, glm5next, OpenPangu) have their own open PRs and are not changed here.

## Duplicate-work check
Open/merged PRs searched for Qwen backends, `max_frames`, `media_io_kwargs`, and video sampling caps.
- #51969 clamps `num_frames` in `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` only; these samplers ignore `num_frames`.
- #54935 capped GLMGA, not Qwen.
- #55727, #56207, and #56390 target glm5next, Molmo2, and OpenPangu respectively.

## Tests
Existing `TestGLMGASamplingCaps` tests already cover the same clamping pattern on the GLMGA backend. The Qwen backends apply identical class-level `_MAX_FRAMES` / `_MAX_FPS` caps.

items.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Skinny GEMM dispatch for tiny-M decode projections
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

At tiny M (1–4 rows) the dense projections on DeepSeek-V4.1's decode path are dispatch-mismatched: MXFP8 CuTeDSL and BF16 cuBLAS kernels sized for bulk traffic run weight-bound rounds. This PR adds a shape-keyed skinny dispatch table (SM100/B200 only, TP8 shapes) that swaps in the measured winners exactly where they win — a Triton SIMT GEMM for the three MXFP8 projections, CuTe skinny for the BF16 indexer/lm_head projections, and ll_bf16 dotprod for the FP32 compressor scores, 20 (shape, M) cells in total.

Semantics are preserved exactly: MXFP8 candidates keep the per-32-element E8M0 activation scale and FP8 rounding (`round_mx` in the SIMT kernel reproduces the baseline MXFP8 quantization), and FP32 compressor outputs stay FP32. Everything falls back to the original kernels off-table, off-device, non-BF16 input, with LoRA attached, with a bias, or under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. The dispatch runs at model init for the three unquantized BF16 modules (K3/GLM-5.2 quant-method replacement precedent) and at the model-layer call sites for the fused/wo_a/compressor paths, so module forward and any wrappers are untouched off the table.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## What

Fix an engine-startup crash when a sparse-MLA model captures decode batches with **piecewise** cudagraphs (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash, a hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA model):

```log
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Full startup traceback (4x GB300, TP4, `load_format=dummy`; identical with real weights, the capture path does not read weights):

```log
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 988, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 920, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 456, in capture
File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 206, in add_eager
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 1483, in unified_mla_attention_with_output

items.title: [Bugfix] Make hc_expand/hc_contract rank-agnostic
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`hc_pre` / `hc_post` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py` are rank-agnostic — they read `shape[-2:]` as `(hc_mult, hidden_size)` and treat everything before it as outer dims. The two helpers that feed them hardcode rank 2:

```python
def hc_expand(x, n):    return x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n, -1).contiguous()
def hc_contract(x, n):  return x.mean(dim=1)
```

`unsqueeze(1)` only coincides with "second-to-last" for rank-2 input, and `expand` hardcodes three sizes. A model runner that passes bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` or rank-4 `[bs, 1, seq, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — hits:

```
RuntimeError: expand: the requested shape has too few dimensions!
```

`hc_contract` has the matching problem: for rank-3 input, `mean(dim=1)` reduces over the token axis rather than the mHC axis.

Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2.

## Test Plan

`test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic` in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`, CPU-only. Covers rank 2/3/4, checks that `hc_expand` puts the axis second-to-last, and verifies the round-trip `hc_contract(hc_expand(x)) == x` (exact, since `hc_expand` replicates).

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rank_agnostic
```

## Test Result

With the fix, all three ranks pass:

```
3 passed
```

Against the unpatched code:

```
FAILED test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic[4-shape1]   # rank-3
FAILED test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic[4-shape2]   # rank-4
2 failed, 1 passed
```

**The rank-2 case passes both before and after** — that is the evidence CUDA paths are unaffected by this change.

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] Make Glm5NextMoE.forward rank-agnostic
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextMoE.forward` starts with:

```python
num_tokens, hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape
...
return final_hidden_states.view(num_tokens, hidden_dim)
```

which only works for the rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` layout. Model runners that pass bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` in every MoE layer.

The fix flattens on the way in and restores the caller's leading dims on the way out. It deliberately does not broadcast: `sequence_parallel_chunk`, `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` and the `[:num_tokens]` slice inside the block all require tokens to live on dim 0.

No-op for rank-2 input.

items.title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Opt-in per-layer overlapped WRITE-push for disaggregated KV transfer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary / motivation

The stock `NixlConnector` transfers KV as a single, monolithic READ at the end of
prefill, so KV transfer does **not** overlap with prefill compute. On
disaggregated (P/D-split) inference this leaves throughput on the table versus
push-style transports.

This PR adds an **opt-in, per-layer overlapped WRITE-push** path: the prefill
side pushes each layer's KV to the decode worker as soon as that layer is
computed, overlapping KV transfer with the tail of prefill and closing the
throughput gap against push-style connectors — while staying on the open,
standard UCX/NIXL path.

Design notes / rationale live in the commit message and inline docstrings in
`push_worker.py` (module docstring describes the event-driven push pipeline).

## Design

- **Per-layer save hook** (`save_kv_layer`): records a CUDA event per layer and
  enqueues **one RDMA WRITE per KV region off-thread**, so the forward thread is
  never blocked on transfer.
- **Seal** (`wait_for_save`): finalizes the request. A model-agnostic
  **"completeness sweep"** at seal time writes any KV regions **not** covered by
  a per-layer hook (e.g. the GLM-5.1 DSA indexer caches), guaranteeing no stale
  KV is left on the decode side.
- **Scheduler bookkeeping** (`push_scheduler.py`): producer/consumer tracking
  suppresses the monolithic WRITE when layer-wise mode is on, and holds the
  engine loop open until the per-layer WRITEs complete.
- **D-side robustness fixes** (small, independently useful):
  - Seed `remote_*` params on the abort/reject recv path so an aborted/rejected
    request no longer `KeyError`s the EngineCore.
  - Handle `num_external_tokens <= 0` (full prefix-cache hit / no external
    tokens) by flipping `do_remote_prefill` off instead of staging an unseeded
    recv.

## Opt-in & safety

- Gated entirely by env var **`NIXL_LAYERWISE_PUSH`** (plus
  **`NIXL_LAYERWISE_DEFER_TIMEOUT`** for the deferred-write watchdog).

items.title: [Bugfix] Release stale FlashMLA workspace views after growth
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Release obsolete FlashMLA scratch storage when another layer grows the shared workspace.

`FlashMLASparseImpl` keeps constructor-time tensor views in `q_concat_buffer`, `prefill_bf16_workspace`, and, with PCP+DCP, `gathered_kv_workspace`. When `WorkspaceManager` grows its allocation, those views keep the old storage alive. Both buffers remain allocated, reducing the memory available for KV cache.

This change stores shapes and dtypes, reserves capacity during initialization, and reacquires simultaneous views from the current workspace when used. Workspace sizing, tensor layout, and the manager's locking policy remain unchanged.

### Observed impact

We reproduced this on GLM-5.3 with DP/EP64, TP1, MTP1, automatic KV/context sizing, and a 0.95 GPU memory target, using a vLLM 0.29.0-based deployment. Allocator snapshots showed a 5,904 MiB FlashMLA workspace retained alongside a new 6,144 MiB MoE workspace on 18 of 64 ranks. The new allocation was traced to `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._allocate_buffers` during profiling.

The corresponding fix on that deployed version produced these startup measurements:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ranks retaining both allocations | 18 | 0 |
| Minimum KV capacity per rank | 490,816 tokens | 603,904 tokens |
| Total KV capacity across 64 ranks | 36,934,975 tokens | 38,971,455 tokens |

Total allocated memory recovered was **103.78125 GiB**. These are startup allocation measurements, not throughput or model-accuracy results. This PR ports the fix to current upstream and also covers its PCP+DCP gather buffer.

### Duplicate check

Searched open PRs for `flashmla workspace` and `workspace memory leak`, and checked issue #51743 and its linked open PRs. The closest workspace PR, #42856, changes workspace bounds for SM120; it does not release retained views after growth. Issue #51743 concerns runtime padded-Q allocation rather than this retained-storage case. No matching lifetime fix

items.title: [ROCm][Model][DCP] Default Kimi-K3's DCP combine to a2a
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 leaves `dcp_comm_backend` unset, so it gets the `ag_rs` default: `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`. The `a2a` combine is a single `all_to_all_single` and is faster at every token count measured.

Wall ms per combine call, MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI):

| tokens | `ag_rs` | `a2a` | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 0.107 | 0.095 | 1.13x |
| 48 | 0.111 | 0.097 | 1.15x |
| 144 | 0.136 | 0.101 | **1.35x** |

The margin grows with T, and combine runs **per MLA layer per decode step**, so it multiplies by the layer count. Cosine similarity against `ag_rs` was **>= 0.999994** across the sweep.

`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` already does exactly this through the same `set_dcp_defaults` hook, added in #50382. This applies the same treatment to Kimi-K3.

Three deliberate limits on scope:

- **ROCm only.** The hook returns early off ROCm. `a2a` is one `all_to_all_single` against `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`, so which side wins depends on the interconnect, and the numbers above are MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI). No other platform's default is moved by this change. Both branches are covered by tests.

- **`q_replicate` is not set.** `GlmMoeDsa` pairs `a2a` with `q_replicate=True`; that changes weight loading and is an independent question we have not measured, so it is left alone.
- **This changes only the default.** `set_dcp_defaults` fills options the user left unset, so an explicit `--dcp-comm-backend` still wins. A test pins that, because a "default" that silently overrode the flag would be worse than no default at all.

### Note on prefill context parallelism

`a2a` has a known caveat under PCP: #56677 pins `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` for a GLM-5.2 PCP4+DCP4 eval config, and GLM already defaults to `a2a`. The measurements above are **DCP-only, PCP off**; we have not measured `a2a` under PCP. Because this moves only the default, a K3 + PCP configuration can override it the same way that eval config does.

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Recompute unaligned host-import tails locally
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Leave unaligned host-import tails for local prefill

## Problem

NIXL pull advertises the whole prompt as externally computed. The host-only
HiSparse resident manager requires imported prefixes to end on a cache-block
boundary. A 32,019-token prompt with block size 64 therefore raises:

```text
ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.
```

This escapes scheduler admission and kills the decoder engine. It was observed
on unmodified main `a08dffe21534916f218dcc93012dbaa01f942691`, on 1P TP8 + 1D
TP8, two 8xB200 nodes, using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` with HiSparse on D. The
new regression also fails on this patch's base, main
`9d14fd3095eb169044e2da0a2a98dd1f2c77ce22`.

## Change

- For host-only HiSparse pull imports, advertise only complete pages, aligned
  across resident and transferable cache groups.
- Omit the unimported tail from local destinations and remote source lists.
  The remote cap is applied after logical-to-kernel block expansion, before
  prefix-cache suffix matching. Rounding the count alone would shift reads
  toward the remote tail and copy the wrong blocks.
- Let normal local prefill compute the remaining tokens. No truncation of the
  user's prompt and no changes to CUDA-graph or memory-utilization settings.
- Keep notify-only receives valid when no complete block can be imported.

For 32,019 tokens / block size 64, import tokens `[0, 32000)` and compute
`[32000, 32019)` on D. Normal non-HiSparse imports retain their existing behavior.
This targets the P-to-D pull path, not bidirectional D-to-P or push admission.

## Validation

New/targeted regression selection:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'hisparse_import or nixl_hisparse' -q
```

- The original NIXL regression selection on base: **18 failed / 4 passed**.
- Final patched targeted selection, including allocation/resume and DC
